title: What Evidence Would Change Our Mind?
scene: Your team has a reasonable explanation, but you do not want to become too attached to it. You decide in advance what evidence would count against the explanation.
sceneJa: チームとしてもっともらしい説明は持っているが、その説明を支持する証拠だけに注目しないよう、どんな結果が出たら考えを変えるのかをデータ収集前に決めておく場面。

chunks.ja: いくつか証拠があります
私たちの説明を裏付ける
ただ、同時に考えるべきです

chunks.en: what would make us change our minds.
chunks.ja: 何があれば考えを変えるのかを
私たちの考えと一致する
注意を引くようになると
見落とすかもしれません

chunks.en: an important part of the picture.
chunks.ja: 全体像の重要な一部を
私たちの説明に不利な証拠となるのか
さらにデータを集める前に
その考えを検証していることになります

chunks.en: rather than simply looking for reasons
chunks.ja: 単に理由を探すのではなく

questions.question: Which chunking is most natural?
options: what would make us / change our minds
what would / make us change / our minds
what / would make / us change our / minds
questions.explanation: The first version keeps the cause frame and the action in clear meaning groups.

questions.question: What does ‘count against our explanation’ mean?
options: Count as evidence against the explanation
questions.explanation: ‘Count against’ means to be evidence or a consideration that weakens a claim or explanation.

questions.question: Why decide this before collecting more data?
options: To reduce the chance of judging evidence only in a way that supports the existing idea
Because the explanation is already known to be wrong
questions.explanation: Choosing the standard beforehand makes it easier to genuinely test the idea rather than only notice supporting evidence.

speak: Sound curious, not defensive. Contrast ‘supports our explanation’ with ‘change our minds’. In the final sentence, make the contrast between ‘testing the idea’ and ‘looking for reasons to believe it’ clearly audible.
review: Previous session: ask what else you would expect to see if an explanation were correct, then compare that prediction with reality. Useful chunks were ‘what we would expect to see’, ‘whether the pattern matches’, and ‘rethink what we assumed’. Today turns the question around: if the explanation is wrong, what evidence would help us notice?
